answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The mesa report shows the merge explicitly at each signal. Because of that, anyone who spins up 32 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 191 times the capital for one share. Each impostor pays 8 dollars up front. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
